notes.key_messages:
To succeed in this paper candidates need to have completed full syllabus coverage, remember necessary
formulae, make their working clear and use a suitable level of accuracy. Candidates should also possess
the ability to succeed in multi-step and contextual questions.
notes.general_comments:
Most candidates were well prepared for this level of paper and very few questions were not attempted. They
also were very competent at using the calculator.
Skills with algebraic manipulation, transformations, trigonometry, constructions and graphs were well
developed.
Most candidates set out the work clearly and showed sufficient working in the questions which required
showing that a given value was correct.
A few candidates did several steps of the working on a calculator and because the final answer was out of
range failed to earn any marks. If they had shown some of the working they could have earned part marks
for the question.
Some candidates rounded early and again lost marks because their final answer was out of range.
The questions that were particularly well answered were 1, 5, 6, 8 and 9. The only question where many of
the candidates had difficulty was Question 10, the vector question, but even here some candidates scored
full marks.
